- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-10-16 (decided in the design doc)
- **Design doc section:** Status codes and Content-Length (p.18)

## Decision (summary)

400 bad name or a body that ends before Content-Length, 403 disabled type or identity problem, 408 a body that stops arriving, 411 no length, 413 too large, 429 rate limit and storage problems. Every check runs on headers before 100 Continue.

Tomcat sends the 400 and 408 for a broken body itself, when its read of the body fails. The service records the same code, so the log line matches what the phone got.

## Rules for agents

Never return 503, and never read the body before all checks pass.

# The contract for the upload endpoints. OpenApiDocumentTest checks it against RejectionStatusMapper,
# and the parameterized web test sends a request for each response listed here.
#
# Still to add: 429 for the rate limit.
#
# Open: herd-device-api keeps its spec at api/openapi.yaml; confirm with the team whether to
# match that location or keep it in this module.
openapi: 3.0.3
info:
  title: Device log upload service
  version: 1.0.0
  description: |
    Phones upload log files over mTLS through an ALB. The service checks every upload on its
    headers alone, before it reads the body, so a rejected upload costs no bandwidth: a phone
    that sends `Expect: 100-continue` gets the rejection instead of 100 Continue. The checks run
    in this order and the first failure is the answer:

    1. The file name parses (400).
    2. The file type is enabled (403).
    3. The ALB headers identify the caller (403).
    4. The certificate MAC equals the file name MAC, in any case (403).
    5. Content-Length is present (411).
    6. Content-Length is within the type's limit (413).

    Only then does the service read the body, streaming it to S3 with a create-only write. It
    answers 200 once S3 has the whole file, and 429 if S3 refuses or fails the write.

    The service never answers 503. No response has a body.
paths:
  /logs/{file}:
    parameters:
      - name: file
        in: path
        required: true
        description: |
          `<mac>-<type>`, or `<mac>-now-<type>` for an upload the user started. The MAC is
          12 hex digits in any case with no separators. Accepted types: app.log, boot.log
          (both also with now-) and calls.xml. Any other name, or a path with more or fewer
          segments, gets 400.
        schema:
          type: string
          pattern: '^[0-9A-Fa-f]{12}-((now-)?(app|boot)\.log|calls\.xml)$'
        examples:
          appLog:
            value: 0004f2abcdef-app.log
          manualBootLog:
            value: 0004f2abcdef-now-boot.log
    put:
      summary: Upload one log file
      operationId: uploadLog
      parameters:
        - name: Content-Length
          in: header
          required: true
          description: The body size in bytes. A chunked upload has none and gets 411.
          schema:
            type: integer
            format: int64
            minimum: 0
          example: 48213
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/ClientCertSubject'
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/ClientCertIssuer'
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/ClientCertValidity'
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/ClientCertSerialNumber'
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/ClientCertLeaf'
        - $ref: '#/components/parameters/ForwardedFor'
      requestBody:
        required: true
        description: The file, sent as it is. The service does not read it until every check passes.
        content:
          '*/*':
            schema:
              type: string
              format: binary
      responses:
        '200':
          description: |
            S3 has the whole file, stored under a key made from the MAC, the server's UTC receive
            time to the millisecond, and the type.
        '400':
          description: |
            One of:

            - BAD_FILE_NAME: the path after /logs/ is not an accepted file name, for example
              `0004f2abcdef-phone.cfg`, `0004f2abcd-app.log` or `extra/0004f2abcdef-app.log`.
            - BODY_INCOMPLETE: the connection ended before Content-Length bytes arrived. Tomcat
              answers this itself when its read of the body fails, and the service records the
              same code.
        '403':
          description: |
            One of:

            - FILE_TYPE_DISABLED: the type is turned off in `device-logs.file-types`. calls.xml
              is off by default until the privacy review (ADR 0008).
            - UNTRUSTED_IDENTITY: the ALB headers do not identify the caller. A certificate
              header is missing or repeated, the leaf does not parse, its CN is not 12 uppercase
              hex digits or differs from the Subject header, or X-Forwarded-For has no last entry.
            - MAC_MISMATCH: the certificate CN is a different MAC from the file name, for
              example certificate `0004F2ABCDEF` uploading `0004f2000000-app.log`.
        '408':
          description: |
            BODY_TIMEOUT. The body stopped arriving for longer than Tomcat's connection timeout.
            Tomcat answers this itself, and the service records the same code.
        '411':
          description: LENGTH_REQUIRED. The request has no Content-Length, for example because it is chunked.
        '413':
          description: |
            TOO_LARGE. Content-Length is above the type's `max-size` in `device-logs.file-types`,
            10 MB by default.
        '429':
          description: |
            The file may not have been stored. Phones don't retry on 429, and nothing is lost:
            app.log carries its lines into the next upload, and the other files are full copies
            every time. One of:

            - KEY_EXISTS: another file of this type from this phone was stored in the same
              millisecond. Nothing is overwritten, and the next upload gets a new receive time
              (ADR 0011).
            - STORAGE_FAILED: S3 failed the write or it ran past its 60 s deadline. Once the whole
              body was sent, S3 can still commit the object after the deadline. Never 503.
    head:
      summary: Always 404
      description: Each upload stands alone, so there is never a stored file to compare against.
      operationId: headLog
      responses:
        '404':
          description: Always, for any file name.
components:
  parameters:
    ClientCertSubject:
      name: X-Amzn-Mtls-Clientcert-Subject
      in: header
      required: true
      description: Set by the ALB after the mTLS handshake, never by phones. Its CN must equal the leaf CN.
      schema:
        type: string
      example: CN=0004F2ABCDEF,O=Example
    ClientCertIssuer:
      name: X-Amzn-Mtls-Clientcert-Issuer
      in: header
      required: true
      description: Set by the ALB after the mTLS handshake, never by phones.
      schema:
        type: string
    ClientCertValidity:
      name: X-Amzn-Mtls-Clientcert-Validity
      in: header
      required: true
      description: Set by the ALB after the mTLS handshake, never by phones.
      schema:
        type: string
      example: NotBefore=2026-10-23T14:22:34Z;NotAfter=2126-09-29T14:22:34Z
    ClientCertSerialNumber:
      name: X-Amzn-Mtls-Clientcert-Serial-Number
      in: header
      required: true
      description: Set by the ALB after the mTLS handshake, never by phones.
      schema:
        type: string
      example: 03A5B1
    ClientCertLeaf:
      name: X-Amzn-Mtls-Clientcert-Leaf
      in: header
      required: true
      description: |
        Set by the ALB after the mTLS handshake, never by phones. The client certificate as a
        URL-encoded PEM. Its subject CN is the phone MAC in 12 uppercase hex digits.
      schema:
        type: string
    ForwardedFor:
      name: X-Forwarded-For
      in: header
      required: true
      description: The ALB appends the address it saw. Only the last entry is used; earlier ones come from the client.
      schema:
        type: string
      example: 198.51.100.1, 203.0.113.7

content.text:
**Why never 503:** the repo states this as a rule but never gives the reason. ADR 0009 sets it ("Never return 503, and never read the body before all checks pass"), but that ADR is still a stub. Its rationale is in the design doc section "Status codes and Content-Length" (p.18), which isn't in the repo. Everywhere else just repeats the rule: storage failures and overload are 429, and `OpenApiDocumentTest` fails if any operation lists a 503. One guess, which the repo does not state: 429 was picked because phones don't retry on it, so the point may be to avoid a status that would make phones retry. I can't confirm that here.

**Why 429 loses no data:** the 429 may mean the file wasn't stored. Phones don't retry on it, but nothing is lost:
- **app.log** carries its unsent lines into the next upload.
- **The other files** (boot.log, calls.xml) are full copies every time, so the next upload replaces the missed one.
- **The next upload gets a new S3 key** from its own receive time, so it doesn't collide with the failed write.

There's also a timing detail. If the whole body was sent, S3 can still commit the object after the 60 s deadline, so a `STORAGE_FAILED` 429 doesn't always mean the file is missing. For the same reason the S3 client itself never retries: the phone's body can only be read once, and a retry after a lost response would collide with the first create-only write.
